subject: Data residency & region pinning follow-up (Acme Bank)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Huang <sophie.huang@acmebank.com>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@acmebank.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Data residency & region pinning (recap + next steps)

Hi Sophie / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to understand Acme Bank's residency needs. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the right architecture and SOW: 

Recap of what I heard:
- Primary requirement: production data must be pinned to EU region (Frankfurt).
- Backups and snapshots must remain in EU; no backups stored in US by default.
- Cross-region failover allowed for DR only, with explicit encryption-in-transit and at-rest guarantees; need to confirm whether anonymization/pseudonymization is acceptable during failover.
- Retention: logs and audit trails retained for 12 months; model input data (PII) should not be stored beyond inference log retention policy unless explicitly needed for debugging.
- You requested SOC2 Type II and details on key management/bring-your-own-key (BYOK).

Clarifying questions for your team:
1) For "production data pinned to EU": is that for model inputs only, or do you also want model outputs and embeddings pinned to EU?
2) For DR failover to US: what RTO/RPO targets should we assume? Is automated cross-region failover acceptable, or must failover be manual with approval?
3) Can you confirm whether pseudonymization (token hashing) during replication is acceptable for PII if we must replicate to another region for short-term DR?

Next steps I propose:
- I'll send our data residency overview and a short matrix showing what resources can be pinned (compute, storage, backups, logs). Attached is the overview PDF.
- If helpful, I can loop in our Solutions Architect (cc'd on a follow-up) to propose a canary configuration for your pilot.
- Please share any internal checklist items (e.g., approved KMS vendors, compliance contacts).

Are you available for a 30-min technical sync next week (Wed or Thu) with Tom + our SA?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-data-residency-overview.pdf

From: Sophie Huang <sophie.huang@acmebank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Becker <tom.becker@acmebank.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data residency & region pinning (recap + next steps)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the high-level requirements below and answering your questions: 

- Production residency: we require that all raw model inputs and embeddings from production traffic stay in EU. Model outputs that are surfaced to end-users must also be served from EU unless explicitly redacted; we can discuss exceptions.
- Backups/snapshots: must be stored in EU.
- DR failover: allowed to US only as a last-resort DR scenario. During failover any PII must be anonymized/pseudonymized. Automated failover is acceptable if we have an opt-in 30-minute window and we retain the ability to fail back manually. Target RTO is <= 4 hours; RPO <= 15 minutes.
- Retention: logs/audit trails 12 months. Debugging data that contains PII should be retained no longer than 30 days and only after approval from our compliance team.
- Compliance artifacts: please share SOC 2 Type II report and details on KMS/BYOK. We use AWS KMS (eu-west-1) and require audit evidence for key wrapping.

Next steps from our side: I'll send a short internal checklist (security/contact info) by EOD tomorrow and confirm availability for Wed/Thu next week.

Sophie
Senior InfoSec Manager
Acme Bank
sophie.huang@acmebank.com

Hi Logan / Neha —

Forwarding Sophie's reply from earlier. Acme has strict EU residency for production and backups, with DR allowed to US under pseudonymization/anonymization and tight RTO/RPO constraints (RTO <=4h, RPO <=15m). They also requested SOC2 and BYOK details.

Can you two help with:
- A short note describing our region pinning capabilities (compute, storage, backups, logs), and how we support BYOK with AWS KMS (e.g., key wrapping, HSM integration).
- The mechanics of cross-region failover: how automated failover works, how we can implement an opt-in 30-min window, and options for pseudonymization during replication.
- A recommended pilot config (minimal footprint) that pins production to eu-central-1 and has a warmed DR in us-east-1 with encrypted snapshots and anonymization hooks.

I've attached the RedWood overview and the Acme QA checklist (cleared for sharing). Sophie and Tom are cc'd — please keep public-facing language; if you need an internal deep-dive, we can do a separate thread.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Huang <sophie.huang@acmebank.com>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@acmebank.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: Data residency & region pinning (Acme Bank) — need technical answers + proposal

Marissa / Neha / Sophie / Tom —

Thanks — below is a concise, customer-facing summary of how Redwood can meet the requirements and a recommended pilot. Happy to expand into a technical appendix.

1) Region pinning capabilities
- Compute: We support region pinning per-route. Production inference can be constrained to eu-central-1; requests routed to pinned clusters only.
- Storage & backups: Persistent storage and automated snapshots can be pinned to EU. Snapshots are encrypted with customer-managed keys (BYOK supported). We can restrict snapshot copy operations so that no copies leave eu-central-1 unless explicitly authorized for DR.
- Logs & audit trails: Logging can be retained in EU-only logging buckets; we offer log-forwarding policies that enforce EU residency.

2) BYOK / KMS
- We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS) via key-wrapping. Keys remain in the customer's AWS account; Redwood performs envelope encryption and stores wrapped keys. We can provide audit logs for key use and support HSM-backed keys where required.

3) Cross-region DR / failover model
- Warm-standby approach: Keep a scaled-down cluster in us-east-1 receiving only health checks and encrypted metadata. In normal operations, no production requests are served from the DR region.
- Failover mechanics: Automated failover is supported and can be gated with an opt-in 30-min activation window (we will queue failover events for manual approval within the window). Failover will only be allowed if anonymization hooks are enabled; raw PII fields will be hashed/removed prior to cross-region replication.
- RTO/RPO: With the warm-standby setup above we can meet RTO <=4h and RPO <=15m for typical traffic patterns; exact numbers depend on prefix caching and KV cache warming. We'll include realistic estimates in the SOW pilot section.

4) Retention & debugging data
- Audit logs: configurable to 12 months in EU logging buckets.
- Debug snapshots: can be retained for <=30 days with explicit compliance approval and will be stored in EU-only buckets unless redaction/anonymization is applied.

Recommended pilot (30-day):
- Prod: eu-central-1 pinned inference cluster + EU-only storage for logs and snapshots.
- DR: warm-standby us-east-1 cluster with encrypted snapshots, anonymization hooks enabled, and manual failback.
- Keys: Use Acme's AWS KMS in eu-west-1 for production keys; Redwood to perform envelope encryption and provide key-use audit logs.
- Deliverables: architecture diagram, SOC2 excerpt, runbook for failover, signed security checklist.

I'll draft the short architecture diagram and pilot SOW today and share a follow-up doc link. If that looks good, Marissa — let's schedule the technical sync for Wed/Thu next week per Sophie's availability.

— Logan
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai
